title: a bit of xor m n is the per-bit XOR of the corresponding bits of m and n
statement: For every natural m, n, i: testBit(xor(m, n), i) equals the (0/1-valued) XOR combine of testBit(m, i) and testBit(n, i).

formal.statement: ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.testBit (AxNat.xor x0 x1) x2) (Bool.rec.{1} (fun (x3 : Bool) => AxNat) AxNat.zero (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) ((fun (x3 : Bool) => fun (x4 : Bool) => Bool.rec.{1} (fun (x5 : Bool) => Bool) x4 (Bool.rec.{1} (fun (x5 : Bool) => Bool) Bool.true Bool.false x4) x3) (AxNat.beq (AxNat.testBit x0 x2) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (AxNat.beq (AxNat.testBit x1 x2) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)))))))

evidence.supports: Nat.testBit_xor is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- testBit_xor 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.testBit_xor[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type. `nat_theorem_inventory` exits non-zero for a name that does not exist, and `grep -Ec` consumes the pipe so the tested count (expected >= 1) decides the exit status, never `grep -q` under pipefail. Anchored with `[[:space:]]`, never a literal tab, per this ledger's own grep-dialect gotcha. `--release` is mandatory: this tool builds `creal`/`complex`/`cpoint`, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

evidence.supports: At the discriminating instance (m, n) = (5, 3) (binary 101/011, xor 5 3 = 6 = 110), all three meaningfully differing bits (0, 1, 2) check against independently hand-computed values (0, 1, 1), each with a negative control asserting the OTHER bit value does not also def-eq; and the theorem re-derives against a genuinely free (m, n, i) triple, not merely a concrete instance.
evidence.notes: A concrete instantiation alone can hide a defect a symbolic build exposes (and vice versa), so both are checked. The concrete leg checks all three of (5,3)'s differing bits rather than one, since a single bit position could not discriminate a combine with the operands or the two bit-arguments transposed.

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*).

This is the Nat-valued analogue of the per-bit XOR correctness statement Mathlib v4.30 states with `Nat.testBit : Nat -> Bool`. It is registered as its OWN local fact rather than a flip of any pinned `ml430` mirror, for the same reason `F:nat-zero-of-testbit-eq-zero` is: this kernel's `Nat.testBit : Nat -> Nat -> Nat` returns `{0,1}` as a `Nat`, a different codomain from Mathlib's `Bool`-valued `testBit` (see `nat_prelude/binary.rs`'s module doc). No `ml430` fact for this specific statement was found in the ledger at the time this was landed.

This fact is piece (1) of 4 toward `F:ml430-nat-lt-xor-cases-c43a1e85` (`Nat.lt_xor_cases`), which stays `open` -- see that fact and `docs/plan/status/263-nat-testbit-xor.md` for what pieces 2-4 (`exists_most_significant_bit`, `lt_of_testBit`, `xor_assoc`/`xor_xor_cancel`/`xor_ne_zero_iff`) still need. `lt_xor_cases` itself is NOT proved by this fact.

Proved by induction on the bit index `i`, generalizing over BOTH `m` and `n` in the motive (the standard `testBit_le_one`/`sum_testBit_lt` "generalize the OTHER variable" device, widened to two variables since `xor` mixes them): the base case (`i = 0`) reduces via `refl` (`testBit_zero`) to a new low-bit lemma relating `mod (xor m n) 2` to the per-bit combine of `mod m 2`/`mod n 2` (a case split on `m` then `n` via `cases_zero_succ`, generalizing `xor_parity.rs`'s `even_xor_hard_case` step from `Iff Even` to a plain `Eq`); the step case (`i = succ j`) reduces via `refl` (`testBit_succ`) to a new lemma relating `div (xor m n) 2` to `xor (div m 2) (div n 2)`, whose hardest case needs `Nat.bitwise_aux_agree_of_fuel` (fuel-irrelevance) composed with `half_le_predecessor_of_succ` to bridge the recursor's exposed fuel to the canonical fuel `xor`'s own definition uses. See `nat_prelude/testbit_bitwise.rs`'s module doc for the full derivation.
